import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Dataset 'data/customer_segments.csv' not found. Please ensure the file is in the correct directory.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering ---

# Drop rows with missing income
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Filter out a clear outlier for better visualization scale
df = df[df['Income'] < 200000]

# Create a 'Total_Spending' column by summing all 'Mnt' (amount spent) columns
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Create a 'Children_Count' column
df['Children_Count'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create the scatter plot using seaborn
# We use hue to segment data by the number of children
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Children_Count',
    palette='viridis',
    size='Children_Count',
    sizes=(40, 200),
    alpha=0.7,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---

# Set plot title and labels with enhanced formatting
ax.set_title('Customer Spending Power: Income vs. Total Spending by Household Size', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Income', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending (All Categories)', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# Format the axes with dollar signs and thousands separators for readability
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x/1000:.0f}K'))
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x/1000:.0f}K'))
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a regression line to show the general trend
sns.regplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    scatter=False,
    color='#c44e52',
    line_kws={'linestyle':'--', 'linewidth':2},
    ax=ax
)

# Improve the legend
legend = ax.get_legend()
legend.set_title('Number of Children')
for text in legend.get_texts():
    text.set_fontsize('11')
legend.get_title().set_fontsize('12')

# Add an insightful annotation
ax.annotate(
    'General Trend:\nHigher income leads to\nhigher spending',
    xy=(80000, 1500),
    xytext=(120000, 500),
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', arrowstyle="->", connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.1", lw=1.5),
    fontsize=11,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", fc="ivory", ec="gray", lw=1, alpha=0.9)
)

# Add a grid and tighten the layout
ax.grid(linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
